question.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot (2\cdot 2)+(-3)\cdot (-3) \\  & =18+8+9 \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{35}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{35}}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
